brief: THE BET. The town has one storey-height. `eaveFor(x, y)` hands out an eave by REGION — 5.1 for the courtyard's side walls, 5.6 for the gatehouse row, 5.8/6.2 for the north row, 6.6 for the tall terrace, 6.3 for the clock-tower sliver — so every house inside a terrace shares an eave and the skyline is a ruled horizontal line across two thirds of the wide frame. Our own block already knows better: `NEAR_HOUSE 7` / `houseOf(x)` gives the near roof a house index that `SLATES[]`, `nearStack()`, `drawPartyWalls` and `ROOF_FURN`'s `hash(house)` all read. Give the rest of the town the same idea and let the houses differ: a house index for each terrace, and an eave that varies per house — most of them within about half a storey of their band, a few genuinely taller or lower, so the roofline STEPS. What the step then implies is the interesting half and is where the diff goes: a party wall or a gable end where two heights meet, chimneys that no longer sit on one line, the taller houses catching light the low ones do not. A 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. Take the swing.
successLooksLike: In the wide shot the roofline is a stepped silhouette rather than a straight edge, legible at 1600x950 and at 390x844, and the town reads as built by different people at different times. As a genuine rung-4b this MUST move at least one of `structures` / `developed` / `passages` in the census — `structures` is the SUM of the named arrays in __census()'s `structure` block, of which `CHIMNEYS` is one, so a roofline that truly changes shape moves it. If it does not move, what you built is a repaint. Re-pin with `census.mjs --save-baseline` and say so in the entry.
avoid: Do not hand-author a height per house — that is a table, not a system; derive it from `hash(house, k)` so `?seed=` still owns it and the terrace's rhythm survives `wrapVX`'s repeat past the west edge. Do not draw a roof: LAWS says roofs are EMERGENT from footprints, and `vZ` averages the FOUR corner cells, so a step between neighbours will arrive as a one-vertex RAMP unless you decide what a boundary means. Check `project()`'s northward lift before you make anything taller — a cell of height walks a volume ~1.15 rows UP the frame, so a raised house can climb into the row above and swallow what stands behind it. And the church at 7.8 and the clock tower are the skyline's two existing incidents: do not out-scale them.
